reason: Let J_t = (u_1,...,u_m,v_1,...,v_t). Regularity of the concatenated sequence means each J_t is proper and each v_j is a nonzerodivisor on A/J_{j-1}. Passing to B = A/(u_1,...,u_m), if an initial ideal (w_1,...,w_t) in B were all of B, then 1 would lie in J_t, contradiction. And if w_j annihilates a class of x in B/(w_1,...,w_{j-1}), then v_j x lies in J_{j-1}, so x lies in J_{j-1}, hence that class is zero. Thus the images form a regular sequence. In the graded case, (u_1,...,u_m) is homogeneous, so the quotient grading preserves homogeneity and degrees of the images.
